activities.subject: reading
activities.title: Sound Seeds: g o c k

lines.text: G is for goat, g, g, g.
O is for octopus, o, o, o.
C is for cat, and K is for kite,
c and k make the same sound, that's right!

learn.text: Four new sounds! g like a goat: g, g, g. o like an octopus: o, o, o. c and k are twins: they make the same sound, k, like in cat and kite.
learn.say: Four new sounds! G, like goat. O, like octopus. C and K both say k, like cat and kite.

misconceptions.description: Thinks c and k make different sounds.
misconceptions.remedy: c and k are sound twins: both say k, like cat and kite.

misconceptions.description: Confuses g with similar-looking letters such as q or a.
misconceptions.remedy: g has a tail that curls round like a hook.

misconceptions.description: Uses the letter name instead of the sound.
misconceptions.remedy: Say the sound, not the name: g says g, not 'jee'.

items.prompt: Which letter does goat start with?
Which letter does octopus start with?
hints: Make your mouth round like an o.

items.prompt: Cat starts with c. Kite starts with k. Do they start with the same sound?
items.say: Cat. Kite. Do they start with the same sound?
hints: Listen to the very first sound.
items.explanation: c and k make the same sound, k. They are sound twins!

items.prompt: Which picture starts with the k sound?
items.explanation: Cup starts with the k sound, written with a c.

items.prompt: Build the word 'cog'.
hints: What is the first sound in cog?
items.explanation: c, o, g makes cog, a wheel with teeth.

items.prompt: Build the word 'kid'.
items.explanation: k, i, d makes kid. A kid is a baby goat!

activities.subject: reading
activities.title: Sound Seeds: ck e u r

learn.text: ck is two letters that make one sound, k, at the end of words like duck and sock. e says e like egg. u says u like umbrella. r says rrr like a roaring tiger.
learn.say: C K together say k, at the end of duck. E, like egg. U, like umbrella. R, like a roar!

misconceptions.description: Says c and k as two separate sounds.
misconceptions.remedy: ck is a team: two letters, one sound, k.

misconceptions.description: Confuses the short e and i sounds (bed and bid).
misconceptions.remedy: e: open your mouth a little, like egg. i: smile a little, like insect.

misconceptions.description: Confuses the short u and a sounds.
misconceptions.remedy: u is the 'uh' in up and umbrella.

items.prompt: Which letter does egg start with?
Which letter does rabbit start with?
Which word starts with u?
Duck ends with the k sound. Which letters make it?
items.say: Duck. Which letters make the sound at the end?
items.explanation: Duck ends with ck: two letters, one sound.

items.prompt: Build the word 'sock'.
Read the word and pick the picture.

activities.subject: reading
activities.title: Sound Seeds: h b f l

lines.text: H is for hat, h, h, h, puff out some air!
B is for ball, b, b, bounce it everywhere!
F is for fish, fff, fff, fff,
L is for lion, lll, lll, lll!

learn.text: h is a little puff of air, like when you're out of breath: h, h, h. b bounces like a ball: b, b, b. f is like a fish blowing bubbles: fff. l is like a lollipop: lll.
learn.say: H, a little puff of air. B, bounce a ball. F, fff, like a fish. L, lll, like a lollipop.

misconceptions.description: Reverses b and d.
misconceptions.remedy: b: the bat comes first, then the ball. Line first, then the round part.

misconceptions.description: Confuses f and v, which are made in the same place.
misconceptions.remedy: f is just air, like a fish. v buzzes, like a van.

misconceptions.description: Doesn't hear the soft h at the start of a word.
misconceptions.remedy: Hold your hand in front of your mouth: h makes a little puff.

items.prompt: Which letter does hat start with?
items.explanation: Hat starts with h, a little puff of air.

items.prompt: Which letter does fish start with?
hints: Top teeth on your bottom lip and blow.

items.prompt: Which letter does ball start with?
hints: Line first, then the round part.
items.explanation: Ball starts with b. In b, the line comes before the round part.

items.prompt: Which picture starts with l?
hints: Put your tongue behind your top teeth.

items.prompt: Build the word 'bed'.
hints: bed starts with b and ends with d.
items.explanation: b, e, d makes bed. Fun fact: the word bed looks like a bed!

items.prompt: Read the word. Which one says 'fun'?
hints: Look for f at the start.

learn.text: You know lots of sounds now! Say each sound, then push them together fast: h - u - g ... hug! Keep going all the way to the last sound.
learn.say: Say each sound, then push them together. H, u, g. Hug!

misconceptions.description: Reads the first sound then guesses a word.
misconceptions.remedy: Say every sound, all the way to the end.

misconceptions.description: Reads the middle vowel wrongly.
misconceptions.remedy: Look carefully at the middle letter and say its sound.

misconceptions.description: Leaves off the last sound.
misconceptions.remedy: Point under each letter as you say it, right to the end.

items.prompt: h - u - g. Which picture?
items.say: H. U. G. Push the sounds together.
items.explanation: h, u, g blends to hug.

items.prompt: Read the word and pick the picture.
items.say: Read the word, then pick the picture.

items.prompt: Read the word and pick the picture.
Read the word and pick the picture.
items.explanation: d, u, ck makes duck: three sounds, four letters.

items.prompt: Build the word 'fog'.
items.explanation: f, o, g makes fog, a cloud near the ground.

items.prompt: Build the word 'rock'.

activities.subject: reading
activities.title: Sound Seeds: j v w x

learn.text: j says j like jelly and jump. v buzzes like a van: vvv. w is like blowing out a candle: w, w. x is special: it says 'ks', like at the end of box and fox.
learn.say: J, like jump. V, vvv, like a van. W, like blowing a candle. X says ks, like box.

misconceptions.description: Thinks x makes one simple sound like z.
misconceptions.remedy: x says two sounds quickly: k and s, 'ks', like in fox.

misconceptions.description: Confuses v and w.
misconceptions.remedy: v: teeth on your lip and buzz. w: round lips, no teeth.

misconceptions.description: Mixes j with g.
misconceptions.remedy: j is the sound in jump and jam.

items.prompt: Which letter does jam start with?
Which letter does van start with?
hints: Feel the buzz on your lip.
items.explanation: Van starts with v. It buzzes!

items.prompt: Which picture starts with w?
Which letter is at the end of 'box'?
items.say: Box. Which letter makes the ks sound at the end?
items.explanation: Box ends with x, which says 'ks'.

items.prompt: Build the word 'six'.
Read the word. Which one says 'jog'?
items.explanation: j, o, g makes jog: running slowly.

learn.text: y says y like yes and yo-yo. z buzzes like a bee: zzz. q always comes with its friend u, and together they say 'kw', like queen.
learn.say: Y, like yes. Z, zzz, like a bee. Q and U together say kw, like queen.

misconceptions.description: Expects q to appear without u.
misconceptions.remedy: In English words, q nearly always has u with it: qu.

misconceptions.description: Confuses z and s.
misconceptions.remedy: s hisses like a snake. z buzzes like a bee.

misconceptions.description: Says the letter name 'why' instead of the sound.
misconceptions.remedy: y says y, like yes.

items.prompt: Which letter does zip start with?
Which letter does yo-yo start with?
Queen starts with 'kw'. Which letters make that sound?
Which word starts with z?
Build the word 'quiz'.
items.explanation: qu, i, z makes quiz. Three sounds!

items.prompt: Read the word. Which one says 'yes'?
hints: Look for y at the start and s at the end.

learn.text: Some words are tricky: they don't sound the way their letters usually do. We learn them by sight. Our first tricky words: the, to, I, no, go, into.
learn.say: Some words are tricky. We learn them by looking. The. To. I. No. Go. Into.

misconceptions.description: Tries to sound out a tricky word letter by letter (t-h-e).
misconceptions.remedy: Tricky words are learned by sight. Look at the whole word and remember it.

misconceptions.description: Mixes up words that look alike (to, go, no).
misconceptions.remedy: Look at the first letter carefully.

items.prompt: Find the word 'the'.
hints: It starts with t and h.
items.explanation: This is 'the'. We see it in almost every story!

items.prompt: Find the word 'I' (like 'I can jump').
items.say: Find the word: I. Like, I can jump.
hints: It is always a capital letter.
items.explanation: 'I' is one capital letter. It means me!

items.prompt: Find the word 'go'.
items.explanation: go starts with g. Ready, steady, go!

items.prompt: Pick the missing word: 'I went ___ the park.'
items.say: I went, something, the park. Which word?
hints: Read the sentence with each word.
items.explanation: 'I went to the park.' makes sense.

items.prompt: Make the sentence: 'I go into the den.'
items.say: Make the sentence: I go into the den.
hints: Start with the word that means me.
items.explanation: I go into the den. You read three tricky words!

items.prompt: How many times can you see 'the'? 'The cat sat on the mat by the bed.'
hints: Point to each word as you read.

activities.subject: reading
activities.title: Read It Yourself: Fox in a Box

learn.text: This time, YOU read the story! Every word uses sounds you know, plus our tricky words. Point under each word as you read it.

visual.title: Fox in a Box
visual.text: A fox sat in a box. The box had a big red lid. "I can hop!" said the fox. Hop, hop, hop! The fox got on the rug. "I am hot," said the fox. The fox had a sip of milk. Then the fox got back in the box and had a nap.

misconceptions.description: Answered from imagination rather than the story.
misconceptions.remedy: Find the words in the story that tell you.

misconceptions.description: Remembered the event but mixed up a detail.
misconceptions.remedy: Read that part of the story again, slowly.

items.prompt: Where did the fox sit at the start?
items.say: Where did the fox sit at the start?

items.prompt: What colour was the lid?
items.explanation: 'The box had a big red lid.'

items.prompt: Why did the fox have a sip of milk?
items.say: Why did the fox have a sip of milk?
hints: What did the fox say before the milk?
items.explanation: The fox said "I am hot" after hopping, so it had a drink.

items.prompt: How many times does the story say 'Hop'?
Put the story in order.
hints: The nap was at the end.
items.explanation: The fox sat in the box, hopped on the rug, then had a nap.

items.prompt: How do you think the fox felt at the end?
items.say: How do you think the fox felt at the end?
hints: What did the fox do at the end?
items.explanation: The fox got back in its box for a nap, so it felt sleepy and cosy.

learn.text: More tricky words to learn by sight: he, she, we, me, be (the e says its name!), was, you and they.
learn.say: More tricky words. He. She. We. Me. Be. Was. You. They.

misconceptions.description: Sounds out 'was' as w-a-s (rhyming with 'gas').
misconceptions.remedy: 'was' is tricky: it sounds like 'woz'. Learn it by sight.

misconceptions.description: Mixes up he and she.
misconceptions.remedy: she has sh at the start: she, ship, shop.

items.prompt: Find the word 'she'.
Find the word 'we'.
Pick the missing word: 'The dog ___ on the bed.'
items.say: The dog, something, on the bed.
hints: Try each word in the sentence.

items.prompt: Pick the missing word: 'Mum and Dad said ___ can come.'
items.say: Mum and Dad said, something, can come.
hints: Mum AND Dad: more than one person.
items.explanation: 'they' means more than one person: Mum and Dad.

items.prompt: Make the sentence: 'She was in the van.'
items.say: Make the sentence: She was in the van.
hints: Start with the word with a capital letter.

items.prompt: How many tricky words? 'you', 'cat', 'she', 'hop', 'was'
hints: Tricky words can't be sounded out the usual way.
cat and hop can be sounded out.
items.explanation: you, she and was are tricky. cat and hop are sound-it-out words.

lines.text: A and I, they work as a team, ai says ai in the rain!
Two little e's, ee, ee, ee, up in a tree!
I, g, h say igh, look at the stars at night!
O and A say oa, row, row the boat!
Two o's say oo, to the moon and back to you!

learn.text: Vowel teams are letters that work together to make one long sound: ai (rain), ee (tree), igh (night), oa (boat), oo (moon). Spot the team, say its sound, then blend!

misconceptions.description: Reads each vowel separately (r-a-i-n).
misconceptions.remedy: Spot the team first and say one sound: r-ai-n.

misconceptions.description: Uses the short vowel sound instead of the long one (ran for rain).
misconceptions.remedy: Vowel teams usually make a long sound that says the letter's name.

items.prompt: Which vowel team is in 'rain'?
Which vowel team is in 'tree'?
How many sounds are in 'night'? (n - igh - t)
items.explanation: night has 5 letters but only 3 sounds: n, igh, t.

items.prompt: Read the word and pick the picture.
hints: oa says the name of o.

items.prompt: Build the word 'moon'.
Which word does NOT have a vowel team?
hints: Look for ai, ee, igh, oa or oo.
Which word has just one vowel?
items.explanation: sheep (ee), light (igh) and road (oa) have teams. chip has a short i.
